profile: SQLite 3.47.2 with UTF-8, stock pager and schema-version pragmas, ordinary connection and transaction behavior. Prepare-time defensive configuration and pager state are part of the external database interpretation.
scope: PRAGMA application_id, user_version, schema_version, freelist_count and data_version.

Maintenance/Header/HeaderPragma.role: One native read or write of database header metadata or a connection-local data version.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderPragma.structure: An exact database identifier, a closed HeaderCookie or HeaderReadField, and an optional HeaderInteger write operand.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderPragma.conditions: Only HeaderCookie permits a write operand. Analysis must establish an explicit database qualifier or bind implicit access to main. Read-only native fields accept an optional source argument and ignore it.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderPragma.meaning: Read the selected field or request the exact write on the selected database. Writes obey transactions. The schema cookie write opens a write transaction even when native defensive mode suppresses the update.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderPragma.externalInterpretation: Use the same physical database, attachment identity, connection history, defensive mode at SQL preparation, pager state and active transaction.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderPragma.sql: Emit PRAGMA with an absolute quoted database and the native field name. Emit a signed decimal argument only for a write.

Maintenance/Header/HeaderCookie.role: A writable native file header field.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderCookie.structure: One of ApplicationId, UserVersion and SchemaVersion.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderCookie.conditions: Only the three native writable header fields are admitted.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderCookie.meaning: Select a native signed cookie. SchemaVersion additionally follows the native schema cache and defensive rules.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderCookie.sql: Emit application_id, user_version or schema_version as selected.

Maintenance/Header/HeaderReadField.role: A read-only native page count or data version.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderReadField.conditions: Only the two read-only header pragma fields are admitted.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderReadField.meaning: Read the number of free pages or the current connection-local data version of the selected database.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderReadField.sql: Emit freelist_count or data_version as selected without an argument.

Maintenance/Header/HeaderInteger.role: A normalized signed cookie write value.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderInteger.conditions: The inclusive admission range is -2147483648 through 2147483647.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderInteger.meaning: Supply the native signed 32-bit value written to the selected field.
Maintenance/Header/HeaderInteger.sql: Emit a signed decimal integer in the write argument.

rules: An unqualified operation selects main. An explicit known database selects only that native database. An explicit temp target opens the temporary database even when merely reading an empty header.

Writable fields without an argument and all read-only field forms return exactly one integer in a named result column. A writable field with any present argument is a write, even when conversion yields zero. The write returns no columns and has native write-transaction classification.

Use native signed decimal or unsigned hexadecimal integer-prefix conversion on the decoded argument. A decimal sign is accepted. An explicit signed text prefix selects decimal parsing and therefore reads a following hexadecimal-looking value as signed zero. Numeric unary plus has already been removed by the grammar. A decimal or hexadecimal prefix may be followed by other characters. No prefix, initial whitespace or a value outside the signed native range produces zero.

Observe signed schema, user and application cookies at SQLite page-one offsets 40, 60 and 68. Observe the freelist page count at offset 36. Rollback restores the selected cookie and changes to no other cookie are allowed. A defensive schema write retains the original cookie and still takes a write transaction.

A fresh in-memory database has connection-local data version one in these fixtures. An observed external commit advances the reading connection's data version. A commit by the same connection does not advance its own data version. External header changes also appear to another connection.
The pinned runtime's locking, corruption and I/O behavior depends on external state. No concrete node keeps a database, native handle, original argument, parser object or analysis context.
observations: Compare exact result names, typed rows, read and write classification, parameter shape, data changes, selected transaction slot, storage cookie opcode and complete signed operand.

Compare actual SQLite serialized header bytes and row populations of all initialized schemas before, after and after rollback. Observe opening temp without using a read that opens it during measurement.
Run an authored file-backed second-connection sequence for data_version and observe both local and external data and header commits.

finite.identity: All 1920 coordinates, validated by the native input, resolved database and field, literal result, and measured fixture configuration. Pair each analyzed coordinate with its direct structure and native observation.

exploration.domain: Vary signed and unsigned prefixes, Unicode and quoted database identifiers, alternate SQL forms, header counters, reusable transactions and both defensive settings.

negative: Direct setter for the read-only data version
Direct setter for read-only freelist count
faults: Permit a write operand on an immutable read field
Always access main for an attached field
Write the same cookie for all writable fields
Treat invalid source text as a read instead of a write of zero
Parse a negative hexadecimal spelling as a negative integer
open: The header oracle fixes ordinary SQLite pager and file semantics. Unlisted storage error paths, alternate compile-time flags and multi-process access schedules are separate assurance domains.
trust: Pinned SQLite implementation and database file-header format.
Independent prefix corpus and native storage observation through sqlite3_serialize.
Closed field roles, exact distribution and independently replayed finite coordinates.
